We need to identify which couplet has a different concept/message. Need to understand Persian verses.

Option1: "روم هر روز بر طوف دکانش - سر خود را نهم بر آستانه‌اش" Means: I go every day to his shop's storm? Actually "طوف دکانش" maybe "the bustle of his shop". "I put my head at his threshold". Concept: devotion, seeking entrance, maybe love.

Option2: "بر خاک نهم پیش تو سر گر خواهی - وان خاک کنم ز دیده ...". Means: I will put my head on the dust before you if you wish, and that dust will become from my eyes? It's about self-sacrifice, humility.

Option3: "گر بود ای شوخ چشم رای تو بر خون من - بر سرو دیده نهم رأی تو را". Hard to parse. Might be about mocking eyes, blood, etc. Possibly about love with pain.

Option4: "ز آن آمدم که بر سر کوی تو سر نهم - مقبل کسی که در سر...". Means: I came from that (place) that I put my head on your alley, welcoming someone who goes in your alley. Could be about greeting.

We need which one differs conceptually. Let's see themes: 1,2,4 seem about putting head (submission) at someone's threshold/alley/dust, i.e., devotion, humility. 3 mentions "blood" and "eyes" maybe about jealousy or rivalry. So likely option3 is outlier.

Thus answer 3.
